clue.text: Someone of fluid sexuality's bound to become a clergyman

parts.note: a bisexual person is a BI, and the 's adds its S
to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: A remark that a person of flexible sexuality is destined for holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy who oversees a diocese.

clue.text: Skin reportedly has lines and stripes in black and white

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that is heard, spelt differently from the synonym

parts.note: bark is the skin of a tree
an ode is a poem, a set of lines of verse

explanation.surface: A creature whose hide is said to be striped, like a zebra.
explanation.walkthrough: BARK is heard but written BARC, which joins ODE to give the shop-counter code.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar code is a pattern of black and white stripes scanned to identify a product.

clue.text: Has ordered over fifties to make will

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the second
ordered means the letters of the word are put into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties are LL

explanation.surface: Someone arranging something over fifties in order to draw up a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' looks like a noun, a legal document, but it is the verb, so the answer is the auxiliary.
explanation.definitionFit: Shall and will are both auxiliary verbs marking the future tense, used interchangeably.

clue.text: Very busy, one then got off at last

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its last letter, which is taken off

explanation.surface: Someone frantically busy, having finally got off at their stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off at last' strips E, N and T from the ends of the three words, leaving ON, THE and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for being constantly active and busy.

clue.text: Albatrosses both taking turn to incubate brood

indicators.note: turn says the letters taken are then read backwards
taking says the letters are taken from inside the two words together

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pair of albatrosses sharing nest duty in turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' lifts SSESBO from across 'Albatrosses both'; 'turn' reverses it. Draft kept apart from splitting its indicator phrase in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess and to brood both mean to dwell on something over and over in one's mind.

clue.text: Imbecile finally promises end to continuous boom and bust

definitions.note: singular here; the answer is its plural, breasts in general

indicators.note: imbecile, like silly or foolish, signals a disordered set of letters
end to picks the closing letter of the word continuous

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word promises

explanation.surface: A foolish politician promises the end of the economic cycle of boom and bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imbecile' is the anagram signal on S, S and BOOM; 'and' is a link. The blog left the role of 'Imbecile' open.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a woman's chest, and bosoms are breasts, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Cockneys embracing new good causes

indicators.note: embracing means the first word wraps round the letters for new good

parts.note: Cockneys are East Enders, people from the East End of London, written E ENDERS

explanation.surface: Londoners from the East End welcoming a new, worthy cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys come from London's East End; EASTENDERS is also a BBC soap set there.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender something is to bring it about, to cause it.

clue.text: Locate good woman, one in a hundred

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a very good person

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the word for a hundred

parts.note: a ton is a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Finding a truly virtuous woman is a one-in-a-hundred chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To station someone is to position or place them somewhere, a synonym of locate.

clue.text: Is porn mimesis, acting, or an artistic movement?

indicators.note: acting suggests the letters are performing in a new role, rearranged

explanation.surface: A quizzical question of whether pornography's imitation of life could count as an art school.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimesis is imitation of reality in art, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionism was the nineteenth-century painting movement led by Monet and Renoir.

clue.text: Region made up of boundless warm seas

indicators.note: boundless means each word loses its outer letters, its bounds

explanation.surface: A geographical description of a zone made up of endless warm seas.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a zone or tract of land, a synonym for region.

clue.text: Giant lime's monstrous pips

indicators.note: monstrous suggests the letters have been grotesquely deformed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge lime with freakishly large seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The pips are not seeds but the BBC radio beeps marking the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips are the short beeps broadcast on British radio as the hourly time signal.

clue.text: It's of assistance to shepherd or miner, but not king

indicators.note: but not says a letter is taken away from the previous word

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Something helpful to a shepherd or a coal miner, unless he is royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a sheepdog bred to help shepherds herd their flocks.

clue.text: Mills and Boon-style books in modern Greek

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for books goes inside the word for modern Greek

parts.note: Romaic is an old name for the modern Greek vernacular
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Romantic novels translated into contemporary Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Mills and Boon is a British publisher of romance novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Mills and Boon publishes love stories, so a book in their style is a romance.

clue.text: One's up the duff in Room at the Top

indicators.note: duff means faulty or useless, so the letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A pregnancy story set in the classic film about social climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up the duff' is British slang for pregnant, but duff is the anagram signal. Room at the Top is a 1959 film.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is an apartment on the top floor of a building.

clue.text: Severely criticised and curtailed American right to lock up men

indicators.note: lock up means the first part encloses the word for men
curtailed means losing its last letter, its tail

parts.note: the Tea Party is a right-wing movement in US politics
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Critics savaging a cut-back US conservative movement for locking people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear apart someone or their work is an idiom for criticising it savagely.

clue.text: Lib Dem politician reportedly dealt sharp blows

indicators.note: reportedly says the name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Chris Huhne was a Liberal Democrat cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat said to have been on the receiving end of harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn describes something cut with axe strokes, chopped by sharp blows.

clue.text: Lugs first of boats from harbours

indicators.note: from means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: to harbour a grudge is to bear it

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word boats

explanation.surface: Carrying the leading boats out of the harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbours' is a verb, BEARS, and loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugs is informal British slang for ears.

clue.text: Requires guts? Run away!

indicators.note: away says the letter for run goes out

parts.note: entrails are guts, intestines
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gory scene: someone needs courage, then shouts to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that entails a thing involves or necessitates it.

clue.text: Answers to clues published when it's time to go to sleep

parts.note: lights are the answers entered in a crossword grid
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: Crossword solutions printed at bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights out is the bedtime when lamps are switched off in a dormitory or barracks.

clue.text: Funny ha-ha or funny peculiar?

parts.note: the same word funny has two meanings, amusing and strange, which is what this kind of word is

explanation.definitionFit: Words spelt and sounded the same with different meanings are called this.

clue.text: Juan was, we agree, regularly out in the dark

indicators.note: regularly out means every other letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Juan and friends agreeing on something in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for being ignorant or uninformed.

clue.text: Jacques Tati can't keep still

indicators.note: keep says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: The French film comic Jacques Tati is too restless to keep still.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was a French comic film-maker known for physical comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Static and still both describe something not moving.

clue.text: Small island in river, short and narrow

indicators.note: in places the island word inside the shortened river
short says the river loses its last letter

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A small island in a river, briefly described as short and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: An AIT, or eyot, is a river island, a word mostly seen on the Thames; 'short' drops the river's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to make narrow or restricted.

clue.text: Male returning morning after morning with large-breasted creature

indicators.note: after places the reversed morning after the second morning

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, morning

indicators.note: returning means the word for morning is read backwards

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, morning
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A male coming back day after day with a buxom woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammals are animals that suckle their young from mammary glands.

clue.text: Historian losing bet in gambler's paradise

indicators.note: losing says a word is taken away

parts.note: Thomas Babington Macaulay was a Victorian historian
to lay a bet is to wager

explanation.surface: A historian who loses a wager in a gambling hotspot.
explanation.definitionFit: Macau is a Chinese territory famous for its casinos, a gambling centre.

clue.text: Relative's entry into Britain's surprisingly supported by Labour and Tories?

indicators.note: entry into puts the relative into the rearranged letters
surprisingly signals the letters appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: the word and its S taken as letters
pa is a relative, a father; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A family member surprisingly gains entry to Britain with cross-party support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the letters of the place name with its S; the father goes in after the second letter. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartisan means having the support of both main political parties.

clue.text: Bounder boxing hard as result of punch

indicators.note: boxing means the word for bounder encloses the letter for hard

parts.note: a cad is a bounder, a dishonourable man
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in a fight, hard punches flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The punch is not a blow but a hole punch: a chad is the paper bit it removes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chad is the small piece of paper punched out of a card or ballot.

clue.text: When you're caned, cane is something that grabs attention

indicators.note: caned is slang for drunk, and a drunk slurs the s sound into sh

parts.note: a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone beaten with a cane, thinking about the cane itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caned' looks like punished, but it is slang for drunk; slurring STICK gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtick is a comedian's routine or gimmick used to win an audience.

clue.text: Arachne's nothing but crude

parts.note: Arachne is the setter, so Arachne's means I am, shortened
pure means nothing but, as in pure nonsense

explanation.surface: The setter confessing to being coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure and crude both describe something unrefined or contaminated.
